description: Independent per-element mass-fraction ranges (low, high) for each macromolecule pool. Used by metabolism_low_dim.model.sample_element_fractions's 'range' fallback, and always for sugar/membrane_lipid/storage_lipid/metabolite (which have no alternative composition-derived sampler). Elements are sampled independently and uniformly within each range; model.py::_sample_ranged_elements_with_closure rejects and redraws any row whose C+N+O+P sum exceeds 1.0, since mass fractions of real constituents cannot exceed the whole. Sources for these bounds are not yet cited in this file.

notes.metabolite: N and P are sampled independently within this pool, but real metabolites don't co-vary that way: N-rich ones (free amino acids, e.g. glutamine at 19.2% N by formula C5H10N2O3) are typically P-free, while P-rich ones (nucleotide triphosphates, e.g. ATP at 18.3% P) have moderate N (13.8%). The N ceiling (was 0.10) and P floor (was 0.08) were both too tight to represent either extreme realistically -- the P floor in particular forced every sample to carry P even when metabolite mass was being used to add N, which is not how real amino-acid-dominated metabolite pools behave. Widened after checking against Makino et al. (2003) E. coli data, which required both a higher N ceiling and a near-zero P floor to be reachable by the sampler.
